title: Typed IEEE-754 evidence-envelope cross-language development probe
question: Can independent Python and Node implementations replace unstable decimal JSON number spelling with a typed IEEE-754 binary64 hexadecimal envelope, recompute identical hashes for every retained D12 reconstructor report body, and demonstrate exact measurement equality for every corresponding Python/Node cell?

inputs.reusePolicy: retained D12 reports are permitted only for development diagnosis; no D12 verdict or file changes

envelope.objectKeys: Unicode scalar strings sorted by code point; current corpus additionally requires ASCII keys
envelope.strings: UTF-8 JSON strings; reject unpaired surrogates
envelope.numbers: reject nonfinite and |integer value| > 2^53-1; convert every JSON number, including integral-valued numbers, to object {"$f64be":"hhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh"}
envelope.floatingEncoding: IEEE-754 binary64, network byte order, lowercase 16 hexadecimal digits
envelope.serialization: UTF-8 JSON, keys sorted, separators comma/colon, no insignificant whitespace

independence.rule: neither encoder may invoke or import the other language implementation; analyzer invokes both CLIs as separate processes and checks their output bytes

adversarialCases: existing $f64be user key remains ordinary data
nonClaims: This development probe does not change the D12 verdict, report files, self-hashes, attack values or static exact failure.
It does not establish RFC 8785/JCS compliance or general canonicalization for arbitrary JSON documents.
It does not authorize a production report schema until a separately preregistered fresh holdout passes.
It makes no Blender rendering, temporal reconstruction or cinematic-quality claim.
